WONDER DAILY GRADE 2 · READING

The quiet work of growing

A bean becomes. · Curiosity day

Name __________________________ Date _______________

A bean rests in an open hand. “Is anything in there?” Inside, a tiny plant waits. Stored food will help it begin before leaves can cook new food.

With water, air, and enough warmth, a root tips out first. It grows down with gravity. A shoot climbs toward light. Two directions from one quiet start.

Leaves unfold in the light. They use light, water, and carbon dioxide from the air to make food. Now the plant can make more of what it needs.

“It looks the same,” says Little Wonderer. Big Wonderer opens the notebook. Yesterday’s mark sits lower than today’s tip. Notes catch slow change.

They look back at the beginning. Did the bean need open leaves to start? Inside, the tiny plant already had stored food — a lunch packed before the first leaf.

They sit by the window. Growing takes time. “What might change next?” Little Wonderer keeps a new question for tomorrow.

Think about it: What helped the bean begin before its leaves opened? How did their notes help them notice growth?
